largeheadline_copy_c.line1: Innovation to a T.

text.text:
Total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA) is a widely accepted procedure intended to provide increased mobility and stability, and to relieve pain. Shoulder hemiarthroplasty, an alternative to TSA, addresses concerns regarding glenoid component loosening. 

Shoulder hemiarthroplasty with metallic humeral heads also presents its own set of limitations, including high revision rates, diminished patient reported outcomes, and potential wear to the cartilage and bone.3,4

Pyrocarbon is an advanced bearing material that has surface properties more similar to bone than traditional orthopaedic metallic bearing surfaces.5,6,7 

Pyrocarbon is supported by in-vitro data to show biocompatibility and the potential for less glenoid erosion than cobalt chrome hemiarthroplasty.8

Pyrocarbon exhibited good clinical function and minimal radiographic glenoid erosion at the mid-term mark.9 

Stryker’s Tornier Pyrocarbon Humeral Head is the first and only (as of April 2026) FDA-cleared pyrocarbon-bearing material for shoulder hemiarthroplasty and is cleared for use in anatomic shoulder hemiarthroplasty with the Tornier Flex Shoulder system. It adds another option for patients with severe shoulder arthritis, addressing challenges like socket component loosening, which is sometimes seen with total anatomic arthroplasty devices.10

Ready to explore Pyrocarbon for your patients?

Elevate your shoulder arthroplasty outcomes with the Tornier Pyrocarbon Humeral Head. Contact our team for surgical guides, case studies, product demos, or personalized consultations.

1.bullet: Pyrocarbon has a modulus of elasticity more similar to bone than traditional orthopedic humeral heads1,2

2.bullet: When articulating against bone, Pyrocarbon has been shown to form new interpositional cartilage-like tissue3

3.bullet: Pyrocarbon has material properties that have demonstrated a high mechanical resistance to wear4

4.bullet: Pyrocarbon has been used internationally for orthopedic procedures since the 1990s, and Stryker successfully completed an IDE for shoulder hemi-arthroplasty clearance in the United States

rte.text:
Key features

  • Pyrocarbon has a modulus of elasticity more similar to bone than traditional orthopedic humeral heads1,2       
  • When compared to cobalt chrome, in vitro (benchtop/mechanical) testing has shown pyrocarbon may have favorable wear characteristics3
  • Pyrocarbon is a material that has been used internationally for orthopedic procedures since the 1980s4, and Stryker successfully completed an IDE (premarket human clinical trial) for shoulder hemi-arthroplasty clearance in the United States
